create.name: Centro Zen Firenze – Shinnyoji
create.bio:
Shinnyoji, the Temple of Truth As It Is, is a Soto Zen temple in Florence founded in September 2004 by Rev. Anna Maria Shinnyo Marradi and run through the cultural association Centro Zen Firenze. Her teacher, Ryushin Azuma Roshi, a former abbot of Daijoji monastery in Kanazawa, recognised it as Daijoji's Italian branch temple, and it is registered with the Soto school in Japan, the Italian Buddhist Union and the European Buddhist Union. Marradi received Dharma transmission in 2008, was appointed a Soto Zen missionary teacher for Europe in 2013 and serves as a minister of religion for the Italian Buddhist Union. She is also a musician, and music has long been part of the temple's life.

The temple door is open to anyone, whatever their belief or commitment, for zazen on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday evenings, with online participation on request, a weekly sitting in Bologna and a sesshin or zazenkai each month. A guesthouse hosts visitors by arrangement with the teacher. Shinnyoji runs talks with the University of Florence on Japanese culture and Buddhism, interfaith conferences and ceremonies such as Vesak. Marradi has co-edited the first Italian translation of Dogen's Shobogenzo Zuimonki, and her podcast and YouTube channel carry short teachings, teisho and conference talks.

courses.title: Orari di pratica – Zazen settimanale e sesshin
courses.description: Weekly zazen at the Florence temple on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday evenings, with online participation on request, a Monday sitting in Bologna by booking, and a sesshin or zazenkai once a month.

courses.title: Ciclo di incontri in collaborazione con UniFi
courses.description: An evening talk in a series with the University of Florence on Japanese language, culture and Buddhism; this session looks at change and encounter in Tibetan Buddhism, with Matteo Miele and Shinnyo Marradi. Free entry, booking required.

free_resources.title: Al cuore dello Zen – Podcast
free_resources.description: A podcast of short reflections by Shinnyo Marradi, begun for the temple's twentieth anniversary, on themes such as courage, gratitude, impermanence and wonder, drawing on the Soto Zen tradition; now in its second series.
